newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher after interest rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher after interest rate cut.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed slightly higher on Tuesday after the Bank of Israel lowered its key lending rate, traders said.
After the close of trading on Monday the central bank said it was cutting its key lending rate for March by 0.3 percentage point to an annualised 13.9 percent.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.07 pct at 103.2
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.06 pct at 102.34
Volume was low at 129 million shekels with most of the trading concentrated in the Makams and unlinked bonds.

"The rate cut was within expectations and the response was very moderate," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel (FIBI). "CPI-linked short bonds rose and long bonds fell. Inflation-linked bonds are expected to remain stable in the near term."

"Unlinked bonds and Makams posted mild gains following the rate decision, which was in line with market's forecast. The market is very stable and yields on unlinked bonds will remain around 14 percent," said Izik Winish of Capital Securities.
"Since the beginning of the year all bonds, except Makams, have risen three percent, which shows that the market has not received significant (new) economic data," the FIBI trader said.

Dollar-linked bonds fell sharply, which traders said followed the decline of the dollar on Monday in the local forex market. The representative rate for the dollar fixed at 3.3390 shekels against 3.3420 shekels on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
